text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says parliamentary elections could be brought forward two months to September.
- King Hussein and German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel discuss latest developments in Middle East peace process.
- Central Bank forms committee to run Amman Investment Bank .
- Crown Prince Hassan to give important speech in London on investment in Mediterranean basin.
- King Hussein holds talks with outgoing Israeli ambassador Shimon Shamir.
- Engineers suspend their protest action for 60 days.
- Ensour says cabinet reshuffle to take place end of March or early April.
- Qatar's crown prince in Amman today at the invitation of King Hussein and Crown Prince Hassan.
- Lebanon bars Jordanian tomatoes from its markets.
- Central Bank takes over running of Amman Investment Bank.
- Crown Prince Hassan meets Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz.
- Amman stock market capitalisation is 3.5 billion dinars ($4.9 billion) and will increase over next two years with addition of 200 companies to be listed on the exchange, deputy bourse chief says.
- Crown Prince reviews peace process with EU envoy.
- Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Khaled Madadha resigned for personal reasons and Kabariti is likely to accept his resignation, official sources say.
